A side-view cross-section (sagittal section) of the human head showing the speech organs, in a clean flat style with soft pinks for the tongue and lips, light beige for the teeth, and pale grey for bone. Show: upper and lower lips, upper and lower teeth, the alveolar ridge (the bump just behind the upper front teeth), the hard palate, the soft palate (velum) with the uvula hanging at its end, the tongue (with tip, blade, front and back marked as zones), the pharynx, the larynx with the vocal cords, the nasal cavity above, and the oral cavity. Small numbered dots on each place of articulation, with labels: "1 Lips (bilabial)", "2 Lower lip + upper teeth (labiodental)", "3 Teeth (dental)", "4 Alveolar ridge (alveolar)", "5 Behind the alveolar ridge (post-alveolar / palato-alveolar)", "6 Hard palate (palatal)", "7 Soft palate (velar)", "8 Vocal cords / glottis (glottal)". White background, like a modern textbook.

Two front-and-side views of the mouth comparing /s/ and /ʃ/. Left: /s/ as in "see", lips spread slightly in a smile, side view showing the tongue tip close to the alveolar ridge with a narrow groove, small straight arrows for a sharp jet of air. Right: /ʃ/ as in "she", lips rounded and pushed forward, side view showing the tongue blade raised just behind the alveolar ridge (further back than for /s/), with a wider stream of air shown by softer arrows. Clean flat educational illustration, white background.

A clean, spacious 6-row by 1-column classification chart of English consonants on a plain white background. Six large, equal rectangular cards stacked vertically with wide spacing between them. Each card has a short bold header on the left and standard letters on the right:

1. Plosive: p, b, t, d, k, g
2. Fricative: f, v, th, dh, s, z, sh, zh, h
3. Affricate: ch, j
4. Nasal: m, n, ng
5. Lateral: l
6. Approximant: r, w, y

Crisp black text, no IPA symbols, no example words, no cell grids, no color coding, no legend. High contrast, perfectly centered layout with ample padding around all text.
